throughLine: Every section is a record with its source attached: the measured thing on one side, the people who went and measured it on the other, and where the record is missing the page leaves the hole showing. Nothing appears on this page that is not evidence — which is why the two decorative mustard "ghost" blobs in the timeline are deleted, not restyled, and why no section may add an ornament that does not name a source, a date, a place or a person.
groundRhythm:
THE SEQUENCE, top to bottom. Hex values are literal; use these and no others.

1 hero            #0D0D0B  black
2 ticker          #151512  alternate dark
3 statement       #0D0D0B  black
4 journeys        #F3F2F0  paper
5 work            #0D0D0B  black
6 timeline        #ECEBE8  paper-2   ← THE PAUSE
7 impact          #151512  alternate dark
8 farm            #0D0D0B  black
9 green the map   #151512  alternate dark
10 record         #F3F2F0  paper
11 give           #E1A32B  mustard
12 footer         #151512  alternate dark

WHY IT BREATHES THIS WAY.
Today the page runs 4,295px of unbroken dark before the first off-white — hero 1029 + ticker 119 + journeys 1115 + work 2132. That is five screens of black before the reader is allowed to exhale, and it is the whole reason the middle of the page feels like soup. The relief now arrives at ~2,300px, right after the statement, which is where the argument turns anyway: the top three bands are the instrument (a reading, more readings, and the sentence about readings), and paper begins the moment the page stops measuring and starts talking about people.

After that it strictly alternates dark/paper/dark/paper with one deliberate irregularity: bands 7-8-9 run dark, black, dark. That run is legal because weight, not hex, carries the rhythm there — impact is the only picture-free band on the page (pure numerals), farm opens with an edge-to-edge photograph on its very first pixel, and Green the Map is a 300px strip. Type wall → photograph → whisper is a harder cut than any colour change would be. No two adjacent bands share a hex anywhere on the page; check it mechanically.

THE PAUSE is band 6, the timeline, and it is enforced by subtraction, not by air: no signal hue, no full-bleed, no halftone, no Archivo display headline (it opens in Newsreader 300), and — the operative rule — NO CALL TO ACTION ANYWHERE IN IT. It is the only section on the page with nothing to click. That is what makes it a rest rather than another stop.

THE HUE BAND RULE, restated so nine people apply it identically. The rule governs the two DATA hues only: RED (a published legal limit broken) and GREEN (what has been recovered). Never in the same band, never in adjacent bands. Red lives in band 1. Green lives in band 7. Five bands apart. Mustard is not a band hue — it is the interface layer, it marks a human act, and it appears in any band that contains an act. It becomes a ground exactly once, at band 11, and nowhere else on the site.

THE TICKER IS NOT A BAND. It is a rule between bands — chrome, like the nav. It is the only element exempt from the red/green adjacency rule, because it summarises every situation at once and its colours are data, not design. To earn the exemption it must be visually caged: its own hex, a hairline top and bottom, micro-scale type throughout, and never any mustard.

WHAT MOVES OFF ITS CURRENT GROUND, and why:
— Journeys, dark → PAPER. It is the longest continuous reading on the page (four routes with descriptions). Black-and-white photographs printed on off-white read as contact prints, which is exactly what this organisation's material is.
— Record, dark → PAPER. The archive is paper. Putting the site's actual claim on off-white makes the claim physical.
— Green the Map, PAPER → alternate dark. It is currently the brightest ground on the page, which contradicts its own copy ("deliberately quieter than the one above it"). Quieter means dimmer and smaller, not brighter and equal.
— Impact, stays dark but changes hex to #151512 so it does not sit hex-identical beside the farm hero.

HALFTONE, counted. The dot screen appears on exactly THREE photographs: hero, statement, farm. Definition of a full-bleed hero, so nobody has to guess: a photograph that runs edge to edge, carries a display headline inside its frame, and has no other content in that frame. Three of them, roughly at 0%, 25% and 70% down the page. Every other image on the site is contained and never halftoned.
spaceRules:
THE ROOT DEFECT: `--pad: clamp(44px,5.6vw,88px)` is a single token applied by `section{padding:var(--pad) 0}` to every band. A 526px mustard ask and a 2,132px project index currently get identical top and bottom padding. That is why nothing on this page has a weight. Replace it with four tiers.

VERTICAL TIERS (top/bottom section padding; parenthesis is the 375 value):
  T1 ARRIVAL   0 / 0                              heroes: hero, statement, farm — the photograph runs to the seam; content sits on its own inner padding
  T2 MAJOR     clamp(88px, 9vw, 136px)   (56px)   journeys, work, timeline, record
  T3 MINOR     clamp(64px, 6.5vw, 96px)  (44px)   impact, give
  T4 STRIP     clamp(28px, 3vw, 44px)    (22px)   ticker, green the map, footer
T2:T4 is roughly 3:1 — wide enough to read as intent.

THREE INTERNAL GAPS. Only three. If you need a fourth you are inventing a pattern the page does not have.
  headline → its lead/body   clamp(18px, 1.6vw, 28px)
  block → block             clamp(36px, 4vw, 64px)     (head group → grid, grid → button)
  row → row inside a grid   clamp(24px, 2.6vw, 40px)

CONTAINERS. `.wide` (max 1580) is currently used for everything, so at 1440 all content runs the full viewport minus a 46px gutter and the page reads like a spreadsheet. Two containers from now on:
  `.wide`  max-width 1580  — image grids, the ticker, the archive contact sheet, hero furniture. Indexes, not reading.
  `.wrap`  max-width 1240  — EVERYTHING containing sentences. It already exists in the CSS and is unused on this page. Revive it. At 1440 it leaves 100px of true margin each side.
  `--gut: clamp(20px, 3.4vw, 46px)` — raise the mobile floor from 16 to 20. 16px at 375 is an app margin, not a document margin.

GRID. 12 columns / 24px gutter at ≥1024. 6 columns at 768–1023. 4 columns at <768.
STANDARD SECTION OPENER, used by every T2 and T3 band: display headline on columns 1–6, lead paragraph on columns 8–12, baselines aligned at the top. This is what `.im-head` roughly does already — formalise it and use it everywhere so the eight section openings are one gesture.
MEASURE CEILINGS: lead 46ch (already correct), body 68ch, caption 60ch. No exceptions.

WHAT EARNS FULL BLEED. Exactly four things:
  1. The three hero photographs (hero, statement, farm).
  2. The ticker strip and its two hairlines.
  3. A section's ground colour.
  4. The mustard Give band's ground.
EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS CONTAINED — every journey card, every work tile, every timeline cut-out, the Green the Map image, all body copy, all buttons. A contained image's left edge aligns to its container's left edge and never touches the viewport edge. The one licensed exception: the archive contact sheet may run to `.wide` (1580) rather than `.wrap`, because it is an index, not reading.

═══ THE RAIL. One contract, both places it appears. ═══
The known defect is worse than reported, because it fails in two opposite directions from the same broken mechanism. In the hero, `.rail-l>.readout{margin-right:calc(-1*var(--rp) - .28em)}` at a 272px readout pulls the numeral 76px over a rule that is really `.rail-r`'s `border-left` — so the rule slices a third of the way into the "2" of 412. In the timeline the identical intent fails inverted: `.cut-yr` is nested inside `.cut-l`, so the `.rail-l > *` selector never reaches it, and at 1440 the rule floats 215px to the RIGHT of "2000" with nothing between them. Same component, two failures, because the rule is drawn by a fixed-percentage column and the numeral is positioned against it.

Invert the ownership. THE RULE BELONGS TO THE NUMERAL, NOT TO THE COLUMN.
  — Wrap the numeral (`.readout` / `.num` / `.cut-yr`) in an inline-block that shrink-wraps the digits: `width: max-content`.
  — Draw the rule as that wrapper's own `::after`: `position:absolute; left:100%; margin-left:var(--kiss); top/bottom set from the numeral's cap box`.
  — `--kiss: .06em` of the numeral's OWN font-size. One value, nothing else. 16px beside the 272px hero readout, 6px beside the 100px timeline year. It scales with the numeral automatically, so it holds at every viewport width and for every value length — 412, 0.0, 6,890, 14/18.
  — Because the rule sits at `left:100%` of a max-content box, it is geometrically incapable of crossing a digit. That is the point.
  — DELETE `--ovh`, DELETE the negative margins, DELETE `--lw` as a positioning input. `.rail-l` becomes `flex:0 0 auto; width:max-content` with a max-width ceiling only.
  — `.rail-r` draws NO border. Its `padding-left` is measured from the rule, not from the column edge, with a minimum clear distance of 32px at ≥1024 and 24px at 768–1023. That kills the text collision permanently.
  — BREACH changes only the rule's colour and its width (1px → 6px), and it grows AWAY from the numeral so the kiss gap never moves. State must never shift the numeral.
  — The rail does not disappear below 860px. See mobile doctrine.

DEAD SPACE TO RECLAIM (measured at 1440, all of it currently empty):
  hero: ~500px to the left of the readout, because `.rail-l` is right-aligned inside a 56% column. Place the rail group on columns 2–11; do not stretch it across 1,348px.
  farm: ~775px × 200px empty to the right of the lead.
  work: a ~600px hole at the bottom-right of the mosaic and a dead right column below "She Leads Change".
  timeline: ~250px of unused measure at the right of every entry, plus ~400px of vertical emptiness under the 2000 row.
  give: ~110px below the three columns before the seam.
mobileDoctrine:
375 today is 12,296px — 28% TALLER than the 9,579px desktop at a quarter of the width. Nothing changed shape; everything stacked. Journeys alone becomes 2,896px, three and a half screens for four cards, and the journey photographs are physically LARGER at 375 (660px tall) than at 1440 (330px) — the least important images on the page get the most space on the smallest screen. BUDGET: no section may exceed 900px at 375 except the three heroes (one viewport each) and the timeline. Target total ≈ 8,200px.

THE RAIL SURVIVES. It is the site's signature and it currently EVAPORATES at 375 — `@media (max-width:860px)` sets `--ovh:0`, strips the negative margins, and converts the rule into a horizontal `border-top`. Both places it appears — hero and timeline — lose the mark entirely on the platform where most Indian readers will meet this page. Wrong answer. The rail ROTATES, it does not vanish: the numeral goes full-width and left-aligned; the rule becomes a vertical line to its RIGHT, still kissing the last digit at `--kiss`, running from the numeral's cap line down past the unit and verdict beneath it; the account column drops below and is indented to the rule's exact x-position so the reader can see what the line is holding. A breach still swells that line to 6px and to red. Same mark, re-shaped.

WHAT CHANGES SHAPE RATHER THAN STACKING:
  — JOURNEYS: does not stack. Horizontal snap-scroll rail, one card per screen width minus a 40px peek of the next, controls in the thumb zone. 2,896px → ~620px. The single biggest win on the page.
  — WORK: the mosaic dies at 375. It becomes a numbered LIST — eight rows of 64×64 thumbnail + title + kind. A staggered mosaic at 375 is noise; a list is a list. ~560px.
  — TIMELINE: the rail becomes one continuous vertical line down the section's left edge with the four years hanging off it; cut-outs shrink to 96px and sit INLINE with the year, not stacked above it.
  — HERO: the readout plus rail owns the top half of the screen; the why + bands + provenance is one scrolling block beneath. Do not stack them as two equal cards.
  — ARCHIVE SHEET: the current 375 version (4 columns × rows, holes clearly readable) is BETTER than the desktop 105px strip. Port the mobile logic UPWARD into the desktop redesign; do not stack the desktop one down.
  — IMPACT: the 2×2 grid at 375 is already correct. Keep it verbatim.
  — FOOTER: currently 856px, 2.5× its desktop height and taller than impact or farm. Two-column link grid, not four stacked. Target ≤420px.

WHAT IS CUT AT 375, decided once so nine people do not each decide it:
  — The statement band's two body paragraphs (they move into journeys at every width anyway — approved copy moved, not rewritten). At 375 the statement is a photograph, one sentence, nothing else.
  — Green the Map's tote image. At 375 that section is four lines and a link.
  — The hero's `.hmeta` provenance block collapses to one line: source + hour. The full provenance already lives on the situation page.
  — Both `cut-ghost` decorative shapes — gone at every width, but they are unforgivable here.
  — NOTHING ELSE. The archive caption ("The holes stay in the sheet until they are filled") stays; it is the point. The timeline method note stays. Cutting copy is not the mobile strategy — changing shape is.

THE THUMB. The bottom 180px of the viewport.
  — The sticky nav loses its second row. 107px of permanent chrome on an 812px screen is 13% of the viewport, and the chip row is currently clipped mid-word at the right edge with no affordance. One 56px row: wordmark left, GIVE right. That GIVE is the page's one persistent thumb target; it is a reach compromise and it is accepted because it is a single target and the same act repeats in the mustard band at the end.
  — Every horizontal scroller puts its controls — tabs, counter, arrows — in the bottom 180px of its own frame, never at the top. That means moving the hero's `.rig-bar` from above the fold-line to under it.
  — Primary actions (Give monthly, Visit the farm, Open the archive, The full instrument) are full-width, minimum 48px tall, never side by side.

TWO KNOWN COLLISIONS TO FIX AT 375: "WHAT IS RUNNING" currently overlaps the last journey card's caption ("Living in a village long enough to stop being a visitor" runs under the headline); and the timeline body text is grey-on-paper at a contrast that does not survive a phone screen outdoors — take timeline body to `--ink-2` minimum.

HORIZONTAL OVERFLOW IS A BUG, with exactly two licensed exceptions: the ticker and the journeys rail. Both must show a hard 8px ground-coloured fade at the right edge so it is obvious there is more. The ticker currently clips "512mm" mid-word with no fade. Everything else must be clean.

TYPE AT 375. The `6.2rem` readout floor (99px) is correct — do not go below it. The `2.7rem` d1 floor (43px) is correct — do not go above it. The approved 14.9:1 display-to-body ratio is a desktop ratio; at 375 the working ratios are 99:18 for readouts and 43:18 for headlines. Never solve a mobile problem by making type bigger. Solve it by cutting the frame. ══ AMENDED 21 August 2026 (client ruling D-09.7): THE 900px PER-BAND PHONE CAP NOW LICENSES `record` BY NAME. Its old licence list — 'the three heroes and the timeline' — lost the timeline band when AD-07 replaced bands 3–6, leaving that exception vacant. Record is the page's register band and its archive sheet is 27 years of cells; it measures 1,393.5px at 375 and cannot reach 900 without either unfilling the archive (forbidden by D-07.14) or deleting the band's living-record half — deleting all three doors still leaves it at 946px. The cap was art-director doctrine, never a client ruling; the client has licensed the band rather than damage it. Also stale in this file: '375 today is 12,296px' — the frozen page is 10,282px at 375 and 10,852px at 1440.

perSection.mobile: Rail rotates: numeral full-width left, rule vertical to its right, account block below indented to the rule's x. The slider becomes a swipe deck with tabs, counter and arrows moved into the bottom 180px. Provenance collapses to one line. The `.rig-bar` moves below the fold-line, not above it.

perSection.job: Turn the data into a body. This is the hinge of the whole page: the sentence that justifies the organisation existing at all.

perSection.ground: #0D0D0B black. Halftone hero 2 of 3. No signal hue. T1 padding. Split it out of `#journeys`, which currently fuses statement and journeys into one 1,115px block.

perSection.mobile: Photograph to 62vh, the sentence set inside its lower third on the `.duo-dim` ramp, no body copy, no button. One screen, one sentence. The two approved paragraphs currently here move down into journeys at every width — moved, not rewritten.

perSection.job: Four named routes, run with schools and colleges since 2004, and what each one actually is.
perSection.hook: Black-and-white photographs printed on off-white — the page's first paper, reading as a contact print rather than a card deck.
perSection.ground: #F3F2F0 paper. The first relief from black, arriving at ~2,300px instead of the current 4,295px. No signal hue. T2 padding. Receives the two approved paragraphs from the statement band.
perSection.height: tall — 900–1000px. Contained cards on `.wrap` (1240), four across, uniform 3:4 crops. Nothing full-bleed, nothing halftoned.
perSection.mobile: Does not stack. Horizontal snap rail, one card per screen minus a 40px peek, controls in the thumb zone. 2,896px → ~620px — the biggest single reclamation on the page. Card photographs must SHRINK from their current 660px, not grow.

perSection.job: The index of what is running this week. It is an index, not a gallery — 'five projects and five campaigns, in the order they take up our week'.
perSection.hook: One image carries the section — the hand-lettered CLEAN AIR IS OUR RIGHT placard — and the other seven sit behind it at identical weight, so the eye lands once and then reads a list.
perSection.ground: #0D0D0B black. No signal hue; one mustard link at the end. T2 padding — which also fixes the 375 collision where this headline currently overlaps the last journey caption.
perSection.height: medium — 720–820px, down from 2,132px. The staggered mosaic dies: sizes currently encode nothing, and it leaves a ~600px hole at bottom-right and a dead right column. Replace with an even 4×2 grid, every tile the same 4:3, captions on a single baseline.
perSection.mobile: Numbered list — eight rows of 64×64 thumbnail + title + kind. No mosaic, no staggering. ~560px.

perSection.job: Twenty-six years in four entries, told with photographs the archive already holds. This is the page's PAUSE.
perSection.hook: Real cut-outs hanging off an ink rail, and one honest un-cuttable halftoned square at 2007 that the caption openly explains — the page admitting a limit is the most credible thing on it.
perSection.ground: #ECEBE8 paper-2. NO hue whatsoever: strip the mustard from the four entry headings (a heading is not an act), strip the green from 'City to countryside' (a history is not a recovery), and DELETE both `cut-ghost` mustard blobs — one of them currently runs under the 'Still showing up' body text and wrecks its legibility. T2 padding.
perSection.height: tall — 1,300–1,450px, down from 1,785px. THE PAUSE IS ENFORCED BY SUBTRACTION: no signal hue, no full-bleed, no halftone, no Archivo display headline (it opens in Newsreader 300), and NO CALL TO ACTION ANYWHERE — the only section on the page with nothing to click. Fix the rail: `.cut-yr` is nested inside `.cut-l`, so the positioning selector never reaches it and the rule floats 215px right of '2000'. Cut-outs must be true silhouettes, not octagon-clipped rectangles.
perSection.mobile: Single column. The rail becomes one continuous vertical line down the section's left edge with the years hanging off it. Cut-outs to 96px, inline with the year rather than stacked above it. Body text to `--ink-2` minimum — it is currently unreadable on a phone.

perSection.job: The receipts. The structural counterweight to the hero: the hero is one red number, this is four green ones.

perSection.ground: #151512. GREEN band, five bands clear of the hero's red. Note the hex: it must not match the farm hero that follows it. T3 padding.
perSection.height: medium — 620–700px, UP from 529px, because the numbers grow. They are currently ~56px, smaller than the timeline's year numerals and a fifth of the hero readout — the proof is the smallest type on the page. Take them to `--t-num` or above.
perSection.mobile: The existing 2×2 grid is already correct — keep it verbatim, numerals at 64px.

Recrop from the photo library to a frame with sky in it. Reclaim the 775×200px hole to the right of the lead: lead on columns 1–7, and set the acreage and the distance as a `.num` readout on columns 9–12 so the band still speaks the page's language.
